checks.sniffing_safety: Acceptable. 58 is only a dynamic relocation upstream: before this change an input 58 was always an 'unknown relocation' error, and it still is unless it sits on lp.setupi. For lld, iRelativeRel only reaches .rela.iplt/igotplt entries, never target->relocate, so relocate() is never called with 58 on synthetic data. A genuine 57 (R_RISCV_32_PCREL) sits on a data word. In RELA objects that word holds 0 in place: LLVM MC sets FixedValue=0 for RELA, and GNU as md_apply_fix writes in place only when no relocation remains. A zero word never has opcode 0x7b, so it keeps its upstream handling. I measured this myself: an llvm-mc .eh_frame (R_RISCV_32_PCREL) linked together with a GNU-as loop object gives the FDE pc=1c012260 = h, and every lp field is correct. An eh-only link is byte-identical to the baseline lld. Jump tables use R_RISCV_32 or ADD32/SUB32, not 57. Residual risk (non-blocking): the check is not limited to SHF_EXECINSTR sections. A foreign producer that stored a nonzero addend in place for a RELA R_RISCV_32_PCREL could, about 0.3% of the time for arbitrary data, be misread as a loop field. Upstream's X86 GOT32/GOT32X sniffing also reads bytes without a section check, so this follows precedent. Optional hardening for a later task: also require bits 11:8 == 0 (the GVSoC isa_pulpv2.py decode mask '0000-' for all four lp.* forms), or require an executable section.
checks.encoding: Verified against the GVSoC source (gvsoc/models/cpu/iss/isa_gen/isa_pulpv2.py Format_HL0/HL1, include/isa/pulp_v2.hpp lp_*_exec). HL0 (lp.starti funct3 0, lp.endi 1, lp.setup 4) has an unsigned 12-bit field at bits 31:20. lp.setupi (funct3 5) has an unsigned 5-bit end field at bits 19:15. Loop level L is bit 7. The target is pc + (uimm<<1), so the value is the forward distance in halfwords from the lp.* instruction. The patch matches this. My own GNU-as objects: (a) a.s: 36 lp.* instructions, all four forms on both loop levels. It covers setupi at 4..62 B, setup at 4..8190 B including 4094/4096, and starti/endi at 4/6/8190, with odd-halfword distances made with c.addi. The ld.lld .text is byte-identical to GNU ld. (b) r.s is built with relaxation on and has 'call' inside every loop body, so both linkers really rewrite the fields (the relaxed code is 9916 B in GNU ld and 8798 B in lld, versus 19474 B unrelaxed). My own checker compares each field*2 with the label address minus pc from nm, and checks the L bit: 24/24 correct in the ld.lld output and 24/24 in GNU ld's. The baseline lld fails with 'unknown relocation (58)'. (c) External targets placed with --defsym, lp.setupi/lp.setup/lp.endi: distances 0, 4, 30/4094/4096 and 62/8190 are byte-identical to GNU ld. 64/8192 give 'relocation R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP(I) out of range: N is not in [0, 8191]/[0, 63]'. -2 gives an out-of-range error. 63/8191 give 'improper alignment ... not aligned to 2 bytes'. GNU ld silently wraps these to 0 or 0xfff/0x1f. The other instruction bits (count, rs1, L) are preserved.
checks.relax_issue: Confirmed with the rebuilt branch tools. llvm-mc -mattr=+c,+xpulpv,+relax on logs/20-F027-evidence/t4.s emits no loop relocation. ld.lld relaxes 'call g' to c.jal, and lp.setupi keeps end=7 halfwords (1c01000e) although the real end is 1c010008. This is a pre-existing mc defect and is already filed as BACKLOG B104. F027 does not cause it: the same happens with any lld, because no relocation is emitted. F027 is the lld half of the fix. It does not block this task. Note, though, that clang's driver default is +relax (clang/lib/Driver/ToolChains/Arch/RISCV.cpp:135-137). The GAP9 sweep, sim Makefile and fuzzer all pass -mno-relax, but a user who omits the flag and links with ld.lld relaxation on gets wrong loops. B104 should be prioritised before SDK builds with LLVM (B29).
